core_principles: Purposeful: every message has a clear, understandable objective

clear_framework.name: The CLEAR Review Framework
clear_framework.description: A practical, repeatable quality checklist applied to all workplace correspondence and documentation.

steps.name: Context
steps.question: Is the background and reason for the communication immediately understandable?

steps.name: Language
steps.question: Is the wording simple, professional, plain English, and free from confusing jargon?

steps.name: Evidence
steps.question: Are all facts, figures, dates, milestone statuses, and decisions verified?

steps.name: Action
steps.question: Does the recipient know exactly what action is required, who owns it, and when it is due?

steps.name: Review
steps.question: Have recipient list, tone, attachments, links, and confidentiality boundaries been audited?

responsible_ai_writing.heading: Let AI Improve the Draft. Let People Verify the Facts.
responsible_ai_writing.philosophy: Learn to use AI for clearer professional writing, email editing and meeting-summary drafts while reviewing every fact, date, commitment and recipient. Protect confidential information and maintain human responsibility for workplace communication.
appropriate_uses: Drafting initial outlines for complex correspondence
Rewording awkward sentences and eliminating redundant filler
Adjusting formality from too casual to balanced professional
Structuring meeting notes into preliminary agenda and action drafts
Proofreading grammar, subject-verb agreement, and punctuation
mandatory_human_verification: Recipient names and correct email addresses
Meeting dates, times, and time zone offsets
Financial figures, invoice amounts, and project budgets
Actual confirmed decisions versus ongoing proposals
Assigned task owners and explicitly agreed deadlines
Confidential company information and data privacy boundaries
responsible_ai_writing.hallucination_safeguards: AI frequently invents plausible-sounding dates, task approvals, participant agreements, or commitments. The professional sending or approving the communication remains 100% accountable for its factual accuracy.
responsible_ai_writing.confidentiality_rules: Never paste unredacted company financial statements, employee records, client credentials, or restricted proprietary data into public AI platforms.

portfolio.title: Workplace Communication Toolkit — Professional Writing, Meetings & Team Coordination
portfolio.description: A comprehensive, practical workplace communication toolkit demonstrating mastery of business writing, meeting documentation, stakeholder reporting, professional escalation, and responsible AI verification across an integrated fictional business scenario.

deliverables.name: Component 01: Six Professional Email Scenarios
deliverables.description: Six distinct workplace emails: (1) Initial Professional Introduction/Enquiry, (2) Clarification Request, (3) Meeting Confirmation, (4) Progress Update, (5) Feedback Response, and (6) Action Reminder with CLEAR framework verification.

deliverables.name: Component 02: Two Meeting Agendas
deliverables.description: Two complete meeting agendas: Agenda A for a Weekly Team Coordination meeting and Agenda B for a Project Planning/Review session, specifying objectives, attendees, timeframes, and required decisions.

deliverables.name: Component 03: Two Sets of Meeting Minutes
deliverables.description: Two detailed sets of meeting minutes matching Agendas A and B, accurately separating discussion topics from confirmed decisions, open questions, and next steps.

deliverables.name: Component 04: Written Stakeholder Status Report
deliverables.description: A structured periodic update utilizing the Completed → In Progress → Next → Blockers → Action Required format, featuring verified progress metrics and dependency tracking.

deliverables.name: Component 05: Professional Escalation Message
deliverables.description: An objective escalation message detailing an operational delay, resource blocker, or conflicting instruction with verified facts, business impact, actions taken, and specific decision required.

deliverables.name: Component 06: Simulated Team Meeting
deliverables.description: Active participation in a simulated workplace meeting demonstrating agenda adherence, concise updates, clarification questions, active listening, and decision confirmation.

deliverables.name: Component 07: Documented Action List
deliverables.description: A synchronized action-item log capturing Task ID, actionable verb description, agreed owner, realistic due date, status, dependencies, and review schedule.

deliverables.name: Component 08: Document Review & Verification Record
deliverables.description: Evidence of systematic proofreading, factual audit (names, dates, figures, commitments), confidentiality check, and review of AI-assisted draft improvements.

faq.question: What is Business Communication & Workplace Writing?
faq.answer: It is a practical course covering professional emails, business messages, meetings, status reports, workplace etiquette and responsible AI-assisted communication.

faq.question: Is this course suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, for learners who can already read and write basic English. An approximate A2 level is recommended.

faq.question: What will I learn in four weeks?
faq.answer: You will learn workplace communication fundamentals, professional writing, meeting documentation, stakeholder updates, difficult messages and AI-assisted drafting.

faq.question: Will I learn professional email writing?
faq.answer: Yes. You will write six different workplace email scenarios and practise proofreading and tone adjustment.

faq.question: What types of emails will I practise?
faq.answer: Introductions, information requests, meeting confirmations, status updates, feedback responses and professional follow-ups.

faq.question: Will I learn Microsoft Outlook or Gmail?
faq.answer: You will practise business email workflows using an accessible email platform such as Gmail or Outlook.

faq.question: Will I learn Microsoft Word or Google Docs?
faq.answer: Yes. You will use a document editor to draft, review and format professional communication.

faq.question: Will I learn meeting agendas and minutes?
faq.answer: Yes. The portfolio requires two agendas and two corresponding sets of minutes.

faq.question: Will I participate in a simulated meeting?
faq.answer: Yes. You will complete one team meeting simulation and document its decisions and action items.

faq.question: Will I learn Microsoft Teams or Google Meet?
faq.answer: Yes. The course introduces appropriate meeting participation and remote collaboration using an accessible meeting platform.

faq.question: What is asynchronous communication?
faq.answer: It is communication that does not require participants to respond simultaneously, such as email, shared documents and written status updates.

faq.question: Will I learn status reporting?
faq.answer: Yes. You will prepare a structured written report covering completed work, current tasks, blockers and required actions.

faq.question: Will I learn how to communicate project delays?
faq.answer: Yes. The course includes accurate, professional communication about delays, risks and recovery actions.

faq.question: Will I learn escalation messages?
faq.answer: Yes. You will prepare a professional escalation message with verified facts, impact and a clear request for support or a decision.

faq.question: Will I learn AI-assisted workplace writing?
faq.answer: Yes. AI may be used for reviewed drafting, tone adjustments and document organization.

faq.question: Can I send AI-generated emails without checking them?
faq.answer: No. Professional emails must be checked for facts, recipients, dates, commitments, tone and confidentiality before sending.

faq.question: Are AI meeting notes always accurate?
faq.answer: No. AI-generated notes may be inaccurate or incomplete. Decisions and action items require human verification.

faq.question: Do I need paid Microsoft Copilot or Gemini?
faq.answer: No. Paid AI products are optional, and the core learning pathway uses standard writing and meeting tools.

faq.question: Will this course make me fluent in Business English?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on workplace writing and operational communication, not complete English fluency.

faq.question: Is this useful for fresh graduates?
faq.answer: Yes. It develops practical communication skills relevant to many entry-level office and team-based roles.

faq.question: Is this useful for entrepreneurs?
faq.answer: Yes. Entrepreneurs can use these skills for business correspondence, meeting documentation and stakeholder updates.

faq.question: Is it the same as Professional Spoken English?
faq.answer: No. Professional Spoken English emphasizes speaking skills, while Course 88 emphasizes written workplace communication and meeting coordination.

faq.question: What portfolio will I create?
faq.answer: A Workplace Communication Toolkit containing six emails, two agendas, two minutes, a status report, an escalation message and a documented team meeting.

faq.question: Does the course guarantee a job?
faq.answer: No. It develops professional communication skills but does not guarantee hiring, promotion or salary outcomes.

faq.question: What is the duration and fee?
faq.answer:
The course lasts four weeks, includes 32 guided learning hours and has a listed fee of ₹4,900, subject to Nova Skills' verified pricing and tax policy.
